title: Implementation notes — Slack noteworthy capture and recurring-note patches
subtitle: Implementation complete · 2026-09-18 18:18 CDT
intro: Each item is a decision, deviation, or tradeoff made during implementation. Acknowledge if fine. Discuss to write what should change (free-text). Revert to flag for undo.

groups.label: Phase 2 — Slack policy, mappings, and suggestions

items.title: Bind structured patches to the exact canonical revision

body.Spec said: Keep full-page review compatible while adding bounded structured patches with stale-target rejection, visible diffs, provenance, and Portable Brain validation.
body.What I did: Added UTF-8 byte-range patch contracts, revision-bound review bindings, derived diffs, CLI and MCP input support, explicit edit-and-approve replacement bodies, and portable-history validation against the parent page.
body.Why: A frozen patch plus the expected published digest prevents a Slack update from silently applying to a changed note while preserving the existing reviewed-publication boundary.
body.Risk: Focused Ruff, mypy, and 23 patch/service/portable tests pass. The broader live MCP subprocess test group could not import open_brain in its spawned interpreter in this run, so full repository verification remains a Phase 4 gate.
body.Followup: Phase 2 adds versioned private Slack policy, explicit mappings, and noteworthy-channel suggestions without capturing unapproved channels.

items.title: Keep Slack selection policy private and owner-controlled

body.Spec said: Use CLI-backed versioned private config, the chosen 24-hour and 1/20/20 heuristic defaults, explicit mappings, a separate suggestions list, and no capture from unapproved channels.
body.What I did: Added owner-only versioned policy state, validated channel and canonical-page mappings, suggestion approve and dismiss commands, status counts, and resumable Slack discovery that scores channel activity plus name/topic keywords.
body.Why: The collector remains the only component with provider credentials and scheduling state, while users can review and change mappings through supported CLI commands instead of editing JSON by hand.
body.Risk: Discovery counts bounded history pages and reads channel metadata but does not create capture intakes for unapproved channels. Focused Ruff, whitespace checks, and 24 Slack tests pass; full verification remains a Phase 4 gate.
body.Followup: Phase 3 consumes only approved, mapped Slack captures and creates review proposals without auto-approval.

items.title: Create deterministic review proposals after durable Slack capture

body.Spec said: Group new Slack captures by thread, apply explicit mappings, create one idempotent revision-bound proposal, keep proposal creation default-off, and never auto-approve.
body.What I did: Added an opt-in post-capture proposer that groups available records by Slack thread, selects channel or channel-plus-keyword mappings, renders a bounded source-linked fragment, and calls a typed engine append operation with deterministic delivery identity.
body.Why: The collector can request a safe append without reading canonical paths or constructing page hashes itself. Captures are routed to the target space and the review engine freezes the actual page revision before producing a pending proposal.
body.Risk: No proposal is created until capture receipts are durable. Failed post-processing retries reuse capture IDs and delivery identity; target drift still blocks approval. Focused Ruff, whitespace checks, 15 collector tests, and 2 review-schema tests pass.
body.Followup: Phase 4 documents the commands and approval boundary, runs full verification, and records synthetic acceptance evidence.

items.title: Preserve full-page response compatibility and pass the full gate

body.Spec said: Document the approval boundary, run focused and full verification, and record sanitized synthetic acceptance while leaving real-source acceptance to the owner.
body.What I did: Updated the operator, Slack, review, portability, and privacy docs; recorded 35-test synthetic acceptance; fixed strict typing; and kept patch-only fields out of existing full-page public responses.
body.Why: The exact full-page client contract must remain stable while patch proposals expose their structured operations and diff only when relevant.
body.Risk: Real Slack account acceptance remains owner-run because it needs app registration, consent, and a disposable test channel. No provider data or credentials were committed.
body.Followup: Run the documented real-source matrix with a small owner-selected Slack test channel before treating live provider acceptance as complete.

body.Spec said: Deliver noteworthy-channel discovery and recurring-note patch proposals through the optional collector without granting publication authority.
body.What I did: Completed all four phases. The collector now supports private policy, explicit mappings, pending suggestions, four-hour capture, daily discovery, and revision-bound Slack append proposals that require review approval.
body.Why: The implementation keeps Slack credentials and scheduling outside the core, keeps unapproved channels uncaptured, and keeps canonical writes behind the existing reviewed-publication boundary.
body.Risk: Full local verification passes. Five filesystem-specific tests skip on this Mac, and live Slack acceptance remains an explicit owner-run gate.
body.Followup: Review this decision record, then run the real-source acceptance steps in docs/acceptance/slack-noteworthy.md when a test Slack app is available.
